title: Power Round — Spring 2024 — ARML Power sub-problem rubric

criteria.name: Problem 1
criteria.description: Correct, justified solution to Problem 1 (1 pt). Statement: 1.

criteria.name: Problem 2
criteria.description: Correct, justified solution to Problem 2 (2 pts). Statement: 2. Compute, with explanation, f(1, s).

criteria.name: Problem 3
criteria.description: Correct, justified solution to Problem 3 (2 pts). Statement: 3. Compute, with explanation f(ks, s) where k is any positive integer.

criteria.name: Problem 4
criteria.description: Correct, justified solution to Problem 4 (2 pts). Statement: 4. Explain why, if m is not a multiple of s as in the previous problem, f(m, s)≤ 1/2.

criteria.name: Problem 5
criteria.description: Correct, justified solution to Problem 5 (1 pt). Statement: 5. Any way of dividing m muﬃns fairly among s students leads to muﬃn division tables such as those created by the students to display how they divided 5 muﬃns among 3 students. Explain why the numbers in each column of a muﬃn division table must add to 1.

criteria.name: Problem 6
criteria.description: Correct, justified solution to Problem 6 (2 pts). Statement: 6. Compute, with explanation, the sum of the numbers in any row of a muﬃn division table.

criteria.name: Problem 7
criteria.description: Correct, justified solution to Problem 7 (2 pts). Statement: 7. Explain why, to make the largest possible smallest piece, no muﬃn should be cut into more than two pieces.

criteria.name: Problem 8
criteria.description: Correct, justified solution to Problem 8 (2 pts). Statement: 8. Since, by the previous problem, all muﬃns should be cut into two pieces, there are ten pieces of muﬃns. Use the pigeon-hole principle to show that someone must have a piece that is no larger than 5 /12.

criteria.name: Problem 9
criteria.description: Correct, justified solution to Problem 9 (2 pts). Statement: 9. Create a muﬃn division table that divides 3 muﬃns among 5 students, where no piece of any muﬃn has size less than 1 /4.

criteria.name: Problem 10
criteria.description: Correct, justified solution to Problem 10 (2 pts). Statement: 10. If someone gets a single piece of size 3 /5, explain why someone else must get a piece that is smaller than 1 /4. (Hint: what happens to the other 2 /5 of the muﬃn from which the 3/5 piece was taken?)

criteria.name: Problem 11
criteria.description: Correct, justified solution to Problem 11 (1 pt). Statement: 11. If there is a division where no one gets a piece smaller than 1 /4, explain why no one gets three or more pieces.

criteria.name: Problem 12
criteria.description: Correct, justified solution to Problem 12 (2 pts). Statement: 12. So in any division where the smallest piece is 1 /4 everyone gets exactly two pieces. So the muﬃns are divided into a total of ten pieces. Complete the proof thatf(3, 5) = 1/4.

criteria.name: Problem 13
criteria.description: Correct, justified solution to Problem 13 (3 pts). Statement: 13. Use muﬃn division tables to prove that f(m, s) = m s f(s, m) for all positive integers m and s.

criteria.name: Problem 14
criteria.description: Correct, justified solution to Problem 14 (1 pt). Statement: 14. Explain why if there is some muﬃn that is cut into three or more pieces the upper bound is satisﬁed.

criteria.name: Problem 15
criteria.description: Correct, justified solution to Problem 15 (3 pts). Statement: 15. On the other hand, if every muﬃn is cut into exactly two pieces, there are 2 m pieces of muﬃn. Prove that F C(m, s) is an upper bound for the smallest-sized piece that someone must receive.

criteria.name: Problem 16a
criteria.description: Correct, justified solution to Problem 16a (1 pt). Statement: 16. Prove that the ﬂoor-ceiling upper bound is tight when there are three students and m > 1 is not divisible by three. (Note: F C(1, 3) is undeﬁned, but it is already known that f(1, 3) = 1/3. Similarly, it is already known that f(3k, 3) = 1.) (a) Compute and simplify F C(3k + 1, 3) for k≥ 1.

criteria.name: Problem 16b
criteria.description: Correct, justified solution to Problem 16b (1 pt). Statement: (b) Compute and simplify F C(3k + 2, 3) for k≥ 0.

criteria.name: Problem 16c
criteria.description: Correct, justified solution to Problem 16c (2 pts). Statement: (c) For k≥ 1 describe a division of 3k +1 muﬃns among three students that achieves the upper bound F C(3k + 1, 3) of the smallest required piece.

criteria.name: Problem 16d
criteria.description: Correct, justified solution to Problem 16d (2 pts). Statement: (d) For k≥ 0 describe a division of 3k +2 muﬃns among three students that achieves the upper bound F C(3k + 2, 3) of the smallest required piece.

criteria.name: Problem 17
criteria.description: Correct, justified solution to Problem 17 (2 pts). Statement: 17. Note that F C(11, 5) = 11 /25, but the correct value of f(11, 5) is actually 13 /30 < 11/25. Find a division of 11 muﬃns among 5 students that achieves this value of 11/30 for the smallest piece.

criteria.name: Problem 18
criteria.description: Correct, justified solution to Problem 18 (4 pts). Statement: 18. For a ﬁnal challenge, prove that f(24, 25) = 8/25.
